tunnel.title: SSH Tunnels (Intranet Penetration) New~
tunnel.notConnected: Please connect to a server first
tunnel.whatIs: An SSH tunnel is an encrypted "private pipe" between your PC and the server — no extra firewall ports needed.

scenario.local: Use a server-side service from your PC (most common). Databases like MySQL/Redis usually refuse outside connections. This "brings them to your PC": after creating, your tool connecting to 127.0.0.1:3306 talks to the server's database as if it were local. E.g. Navicat manages the server's MySQL.
scenario.remote: Let the server (or others) reach a service running on your PC — great for demos and debugging. The server listens on a port; anyone visiting ServerIP:port reaches your local service. E.g. a colleague views the dev website running on your laptop.
scenario.dynamic: Turn the server into a secure proxy for your traffic. Set your browser/app proxy to socks5://127.0.0.1:localPort; all requests travel through the encrypted tunnel. E.g. access internal systems only reachable from the server's network.

tunnel.portInUse: Port already in use by another tunnel
tunnel.notePlaceholder: Add a note for this tunnel (optional)
tunnel.quickActions: One-click templates (most common: bring the server's database to your PC):

desc.local:
Forward server data through your local PC.
Example: MySQL on the server uses port 3306.
Set your PC's 127.0.0.1:3306 to forward to the server's port 3306,
then you can use 127.0.0.1:3306 on your PC to connect to the server's MySQL.
desc.remote:
Forward your PC's information through the server — the reverse of local forwarding.
Example: an app on your PC uses port 5555.
Set the server's IP:5555 to forward to your PC's 127.0.0.1:5555,
then anyone can use the server's public IP:5555 to reach the app on your PC running on port 5555.
desc.dynamic: Run a S5 proxy on your PC.

tunnel.empty: No active tunnels. Create one to get started!
tunnel.emptyHint: Use a one-click template above — e.g. forward MySQL, then connect with Navicat to 127.0.0.1:3306.
tunnel.gatewayPortsHint: By default sshd only lets server forwards bind to 127.0.0.1, so the public internet cannot reach them. Enabling makes the server listen on 0.0.0.0 so forwarded ports become publicly reachable. Requires root; it edits /etc/ssh/sshd_config and restarts sshd (existing SSH sessions stay up). ⚠ The toggle only affects newly created tunnels: existing server forwards keep their original bind; recreate them to apply the change.
tunnel.gatewayReconnectHint: Reconnect the server and restart your remote tunnels for it to take effect.
tunnel.gatewayPortsDialogOffWarn: GatewayPorts is off. The tunnel cannot be reached from the public internet — only accessible from 127.0.0.1 on the server
tunnel.gatewayPortsDialogUnknown: Could not detect GatewayPorts (permissions or sshd -T unavailable). You can still try to enable it.
tunnel.gatewayPortsDialogOnWarn: GatewayPorts is enabled — tunnels are publicly reachable. If you want server-forwarded content to be reachable only via 127.0.0.1 on the server,
tunnel.reconnectHint: GatewayPorts is enabled but requires a reconnect to take effect. Reconnecting briefly interrupts this session (terminal, file transfers, existing tunnels). Reconnect now?
tunnel.reconnectRisk: Security note: forwarded ports will listen on 0.0.0.0 and be publicly reachable. Please configure your firewall and access controls.
tunnel.reconnectDone: Reconnected. GatewayPorts is active — recreate your server-forwarding tunnels.
tunnel.reconnectManualHint: GatewayPorts enabled — please disconnect and reconnect the server manually for it to take effect.
tunnel.reconnectHintDisable: GatewayPorts is now disabled but requires a reconnect to take effect. Reconnecting briefly interrupts this session (terminal, file transfers, existing tunnels). Reconnect now?
tunnel.reconnectDoneDisable: Reconnected. GatewayPorts is disabled — server forwards will only accept 127.0.0.1.
tunnel.reconnectManualHintDisable: GatewayPorts disabled — please disconnect and reconnect the server manually for it to take effect.
tunnel.batchDeleteHint: This will permanently delete {{count}} tunnels. Running ones will be stopped first. This cannot be undone!
tunnel.deleteHint: This permanently removes the tunnel configuration — it can no longer be started after a reconnect. Type del to confirm.

errors.connectFailed: The server could not reach {{target}}. Check: ① Is the service running on the server? ② Is the port correct? (run `ss -tlnp` in the server terminal) ③ Is the server address correct? (services usually listen on 127.0.0.1 — don't use the public IP)
errors.prohibited: The server refused the channel forward ({{target}}). Likely cause: SSH forwarding is disabled on the server (AllowTcpForwarding no) — ask the server admin to enable it
errors.localConnectFailed: The server could not reach your local service {{target}}. Check: is it running? Does it listen on 127.0.0.1 or 0.0.0.0? Is the port correct?
errors.socks4: The client sent SOCKS4 traffic (first byte 0x04). Switch the proxy protocol to SOCKS5 — use the socks5:// prefix (some apps treat socks:// as SOCKS4)
errors.httpProxy: The client sent HTTP proxy traffic. Switch the proxy type to SOCKS5. Note: Windows system proxy settings don't support SOCKS5 — configure socks5://127.0.0.1:port inside the browser or app
errors.badGreeting: Unrecognized connection data ({{detail}}). Make sure the client proxy type is SOCKS5

about.title: About LeePanel
about.line1: LeePanel — Free and open-source, the next-generation Linux server management panel.
about.line2: Traditional Linux/VPS management panels frequently suffer from security vulnerabilities, causing endless headaches for server administrators.
about.line3: LeePanel was built to solve this once and for all.
about.line4: 🛡️ Zero server-side code — All operations are performed via SSH commands from your local machine. No panel code installed on the server, no extra ports exposed, eliminating the panel's own security risks at the root.
about.line5: A lightweight cross-platform desktop app built with Tauri 2 + React, providing a single native client to manage: SSH Terminal & SFTP File Management, Nginx / MySQL/MariaDB / PHP / Redis / Docker, Firewall / Free SSL Certificates.
about.line6: Installer as small as 6 MB — lightweight and flexible! Completely replacing traditional browser-based panels.
